newsitem.title: UK: CITGO's Texas refinery on fire after explosion.
newsitem.headline: CITGO's Texas refinery on fire after explosion.

text.p: A fire at CITGO Petroleum Corp's 150,000 barrels per day (bpd) oil refinery in Corpus Christi, Texas, was still burning on Tuesday after an explosion late on Monday, a police spokesman said.
"There was an explosion at the refinery at 2222 (0422 GMT)," Captain Richard Lewinsky of Corpus Christi police told Reuters.
Lewinsky said a refining tower at the plant exploded during a violent thunderstorm. The force of the explosion was enough to shake a police station some three miles away, he said.
No casualties have been reported so far, he said.
He had no information about operations at the refinery, where fire-fighters were still tackling the blaze.
"It's still burning. I believe it's going to be a controlled burn until it goes out," he said.
CITGO Petroleum, based in Tulsa, Oklahoma, is owned by PDV America Inc, an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA), the national oil company of Venezuela.
CITGO officials were not immediately available for comment.
